items: Long-term debt is not reported for Ford in any year, so its long-term debt to equity is n/r; GM reports $131.6B of long-term debt and a 2.15× ratio in FY2025, up from 1.84× in FY2021.
Ford's shareholders' equity fell from $44.8B in FY2024 to $36.0B in FY2025, after a net loss of −$8.2B. GM's equity moved from $63.1B to $61.1B over the same year.
Total liabilities were $253.2B against $289.2B of assets for Ford, and $218.1B against $281.3B for GM, in FY2025.
Cash was close at $23.4B for Ford and $20.9B for GM in FY2025. Cash runway is n/m for both companies in every year.
Ford paid $3.0B in dividends and $0 in buybacks in FY2025. GM paid $657M in dividends and $6.0B in buybacks, and its shares outstanding fell from 1.5B to 904M since FY2021.

Ford vs GM: cushion against a bad year

Both carry large liabilities against cash and equity; the charts show how each balance sheet and cash outflow moved, FY2021 to FY2025.

Ford (F)General Motors (GM)

Cash

Cash trend from a zero baseline; hover for values.

Shareholders' equity

Equity trend from a zero baseline.

What assets are made of

Dark part of each bar is total liabilities; the colored remainder is assets beyond liabilities.

Cash leaving: dividends and buybacks

Solid is dividends paid, lighter is buybacks, by year.

Free cash flow

Cash left after capital expenditure.

Long-term debt to equity

GM reports it each year; Ford's long-term debt is n/r, so its ratio is n/r.

Figures behind the charts

Headline latest-year Cash, Long-term debt, Equity and ratio are shown in the site's strip, so FY2025 is omitted for those rows.

Notes on what is not reported

Ford's long-term debt and long-term debt to equity are n/r in every year, and gross profit is n/r for both companies. GM's R&D is n/r. Cash runway is n/m for both companies in every year, so no runway is shown. Fiscal years end 12-31 for both.

Takeaways

  • Ford's long-term debt is n/r, so its debt-to-equity cannot be set beside GM's, which rose from 1.84× in FY2021.
  • Ford reported a net loss of −$8.2B and operating loss of −$9.2B in FY2025, while GM stayed profitable with net income of $2.7B.
  • GM's buybacks were $11.1B in FY2023, whereas Ford's largest outflow was $5.0B of dividends that year.
  • Ford's free cash flow was −$13.0M in FY2022; GM's was $6.8B the same year.
  • Ford's total liabilities grew from $208.4B in FY2021 to $253.2B in FY2025, and GM's from $178.9B to $218.1B.

Source: each company's 10-K filings, FY2021 to FY2025. Not financial advice.
